scope.description: Complete five-row deepening tranche for the Communication Evolution Campaign source slice, emphasizing Bill's PC / Masaki mail-in mechanics, trade-evolution game logic, Media Factory route, Expansion Sheet 3 launch context, regular-stock-vs-glossy trap, and later Pokemon Web / Wizards reprint pressure.

assembly_themes: later Pokemon Web and Wizards reprint pressure

main_chase_cards.name: Alakazam
main_chase_cards.why: The most-requested campaign card in the card-page data and a perfect match between Kadabra trade-evolution logic and Masaki/Bill mechanics.

main_chase_cards.name: Gengar
main_chase_cards.why: A beloved ghost line, later Pokemon Web pressure, and one of the cards where the campaign idea feels exactly like the video game.

main_chase_cards.name: Machamp
main_chase_cards.why: The later Wizards/Pokemon Web memory makes Machamp a route-discipline test: the same card family can be loud while the Masaki route stays specific.

key_artists.name: Yukiko Baba
key_artists.why: Baba gives the least-requested card its fossil-strange texture; Omastar also proves the campaign was about communication/evolution ritual more than a perfect game-mechanic mirror.

key_artists.name: Shin-ichi Yoshida
key_artists.why: Yoshida's Alakazam sits at the center of the campaign's psychic/intelligence fantasy: a card made obtainable by sending Kadabra through Bill's machine.

key_artists.name: Hironobu Yoshida
key_artists.why: Yoshida's Gengar makes the campaign feel mischievous and haunted, and later Pokemon Web reuse makes exact route discipline essential.

key_artists.name: Nobuyuki Habu
key_artists.why: Habu's Golem gives the campaign its heavy, rocky trade-evolution pole: Graveler mailed away, Golem returned.

key_artists.why: Komiya's Machamp is route-sensitive because collectors may meet the image through Wizards Black Star or Pokemon Web memory; the campaign object still has to be identified by the Japanese mail-in lane.

claims.text: The local source slice models five source-pinned rows for the Communication Evolution Campaign: Omastar 088, Alakazam 089, Gengar 090, Golem 091, and Machamp 092.

The local row carries a mixed-source release date of 1998-11-13, while Bulbapedia card pages say the campaign launched with Expansion Sheet 3 on November 24, 1998 and ran until April 30, 1999. This dossier preserves the caveat rather than flattening the dates.

Card-page release information describes participants mailing the relevant pre-evolution card plus Bill's PC from Vending/Expansion Sheet Series 3 to Media Factory, receiving the evolved card in return.

The campaign matters because it turned Pokemon's most social mechanic into paper ritual: a player did not just pull a trade evolution, they mailed a card through Bill's PC / Masaki and waited for the evolved form to come back.
Bulbapedia trivia notes that Expansion Sheet cards are glossy while Communication Evolution Campaign cards are regular stock; this is an identification rail, not an authentication substitute.

Agents should preserve Communication Evolution / Masaki route, Bill's PC requirement, mailed pre-evolution card, row 088-092 identity, regular-stock campaign distinction, and later Pokemon Web/Wizards reprint pressure before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Communication Evolution Campaign — Bill's machine becomes a mail route
narrative.why_it_matters: This is one of the cleanest examples of Pokemon becoming an apparatus. The Game Boy taught kids that some creatures only become themselves through contact with another player. The campaign turned that rule into paperwork, postage, and waiting: send a pre-evolution and Bill's PC to Media Factory, receive Omastar, Alakazam, Gengar, Golem, or Machamp back. That is why collectors call them Masaki promos. They are not just rare holos; they are the physical memory of communication becoming evolution.

card_highlights.assembly_note: Omastar is row 088 and requires Omanyte plus Bill's PC in the campaign story; it is the interesting exception because Omanyte does not evolve by trade in the video games.
card_highlights.collector_texture_note: Omastar is the campaign's fossil oddity. The whole promotion is about communication becoming evolution, and then Omastar walks in sideways: not a trade evolution in the games, but still pulled through Bill's PC and the mail. That makes it quieter than Alakazam or Gengar, but conceptually delicious.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Omastar as Communication Evolution Campaign source row 088; the card page gives Japanese name オムスター and transliteration Omstar.
The Omastar card page credits Yukiko Baba as illustrator.
The card page says participants mailed any Omanyte card plus Bill's PC to Media Factory and received Omastar in return.

Omastar matters because it breaks the clean trade-evolution pattern: the fossil line did not require trading in the games, so its presence shows the campaign was a broader Bill's PC ritual, not just a one-to-one game mechanic.
Agents should preserve row 088, Omanyte plus Bill's PC route, Yukiko Baba credit, rare-holo unnumbered promo identity, regular stock, and Omastar's exception status before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Omastar — the fossil exception inside Masaki's machine
narrative.why_it_matters: Omastar is the one that makes the campaign smarter than its slogan. Alakazam, Gengar, Golem, and Machamp all fit the trade-evolution idea cleanly. Omastar does not. So row 088 becomes a fossil-shaped reminder that the ritual mattered too: Bill's PC, a mailed card, Media Factory, and a return object that felt transformed even when the game rule was not exact.

narrative.why_it_matters: Alakazam is the campaign's thesis card. Kadabra is already the creature that wants a connection to become complete, and here the connection is not abstract. It is a card, Bill's PC, an envelope, Media Factory, and a returned holo. The result feels less like a prize than a successful transmission.

card_highlights.assembly_note: Machamp is row 092; its page redirects through Wizards Promo 43, so the agent has to keep Japanese campaign route separate from later English and Pokemon Web memories.
card_highlights.collector_texture_note: Machamp is the campaign's body. Machoke goes into the route, Machamp comes back, and the later English/Wizards fame makes it tempting to think the family is enough. It is not. This object is row 092, Masaki route, Japanese mail-in.

The Machamp page credits Tomokazu Komiya as illustrator for the Wizards/Pokemon Web visible lineage while also identifying the Japanese Unnumbered Promotional print in the expansion table.
The Machamp page says participants mailed any Machoke card plus Bill's PC to Media Factory and received Machamp in return.
The Machamp page routes through Wizards Black Star Promo 43 and notes later Pokemon Web reuse, making route separation essential for this campaign row.

Machamp matters because it is the bodybuilder version of the campaign thesis: Machoke is sent through Bill's PC and returned as the fully evolved force, but later English fame makes exact Japanese route evidence crucial.

Agents should preserve row 092, Machoke plus Bill's PC route, Tomokazu Komiya lineage context, rare-holo unnumbered promo identity, and non-equivalence to Wizards Black Star or Pokemon Web memories before accepting a match.

narrative.why_it_matters: Machamp is almost too easy to recognize, which is why it is dangerous. A collector sees Machamp, Wizards, Pokemon Web, Komiya, and muscle memory fires. The agent has to slow the room down: was this the Japanese Communication Evolution object, row 092, obtained by sending Machoke and Bill's PC through Media Factory? If not, it may be related, but it is not this.
